subject: Washing machine rotten egg smell
query: why does my washing machine smell like rotten eggs
title: Why does my washing machine smell like rotten eggs? Causes and fixes
answer: A rotten egg smell from a washer usually comes from bacteria growing in soap scum, lint and moisture inside the machine or drain, or from sewer gas rising through a dried-out drain trap. Less often, the smell is in the water itself. Important: if the smell is also near a gas dryer, water heater or stove, leave and call your gas company.
body:
Natural gas has a rotten egg odor added on purpose so leaks are noticeable. If you smell it anywhere other than inside the washer, don't use switches or appliances; go outside and call the gas utility or 911.

The most likely causes, from most to least common:

1. Bacteria and mildew inside the washer. Front loaders are most prone, because water sits in the rubber door seal and the drain pump filter. Top loaders collect detergent residue under the tub. Clean the door gasket and detergent drawer, then run the machine's clean cycle, or the hottest normal cycle, with a washer cleaner or chlorine bleach (check your manual for the amount). Never mix bleach with vinegar or ammonia.
2. A clogged drain pump filter (front loaders). It is usually behind a small door at the bottom front. Put down towels and a shallow pan, since water will come out, then unscrew it and clean out lint, coins and slime.
3. A dry drain trap. The U-shaped pipe under the standpipe holds water that blocks sewer gas. If the washer hasn't been used for a few weeks, that water can evaporate. Pour a bucket of water down the standpipe.
4. A clogged drain line or blocked vent. Lint and soap scum can build up in the standpipe, and a blocked plumbing vent can push sewer gas back into the laundry room.
5. Sulfur in the water. Run hot and cold water at a nearby sink. If only hot water smells, the cause is usually the water heater, where sulfur bacteria and the magnesium anode rod produce hydrogen sulfide. If both smell, the gas is likely in your well water. Health officials say the smell alone usually doesn't make water unsafe, but well owners should test for bacteria.

To prevent it, leave the door or lid open after each load, wipe the door seal, use high-efficiency (HE) detergent in the right amount, and run a cleaning cycle about once a month.

When to call a pro: call a plumber if the smell comes from the drain or walls after cleaning, or if the drain keeps backing up. Replacing a water heater's anode rod or sanitizing the heater involves very hot water, so leave it to a plumber. Call an appliance technician if the drain pump or filter housing is damaged.

faq.q: Why does my washer smell like sewage?
faq.a: Usually because the drain trap has dried out, or the drain line or vent is clogged, letting sewer gas into the room. Pour water into the standpipe first; if the smell continues, call a plumber.

faq.q: Why do my clean clothes smell like rotten eggs?
faq.a: Either the washer is growing bacteria that transfer odor to the load, or your hot water contains hydrogen sulfide. Check whether hot tap water smells the same.

faq.q: How do I get the rotten egg smell out of my front-load washer?
faq.a: Clean the rubber door seal and the drain pump filter, then run a hot clean cycle with a washer cleaner or bleach. Leave the door open afterward so it dries.

faq.q: Is a rotten egg smell from a washing machine dangerous?
faq.a: Bacteria in the washer are a nuisance, not a hazard. A gas leak is dangerous: if you smell rotten eggs near gas appliances, leave and call the gas company.

faq.q: Does vinegar get rid of washing machine smell?
faq.a: Vinegar can help with mild odors, but many washer makers recommend a washer cleaner or bleach for bacteria. Never use vinegar and bleach in the same cycle.
